gogpt_prior_assessment: The GOGPT prior 'JiuJiang PXSteel Co., Ltd. power project' (260 MW, 1.72 km away) is Fangda Group's own captive power plant for its Jiujiang PXSteel integrated steel mill (Fangda Jiujiang Steel Gas Power Project) at Hukou High-tech Industrial Park -- a completely different industrial host's on-site generation, unrelated to the never-built LNG terminal. This is the industrial-host trap (SOP): a colocated captive plant belonging to a different port/industrial tenant.
gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT record already exists (JiuJiang PXSteel Co., Ltd. power project) and it is unambiguously the steel mill's own captive plant, not the LNG terminal's -- and the terminal itself was never built.
notes: Screen criterion: cancelled-and-never-built proposal (feasibility-study stage only, no construction). GOGPT proximity match is a false positive -- different host (steel mill), not the terminal.

captive_summary: Grid-fed, no captive power. The Shandong Energy Regulatory Office (national/provincial regulator) reports a dedicated 110kV power-transmission project ('110KV输变电工程') built specifically to supply this terminal from the external grid, alongside the dock works, during construction. The terminal's own EIA approval (Yantai Ecology & Environment Bureau, 烟环审[2019]41号) describes only heat-duty gas combustion (submerged-combustion vaporizers, 浸没燃烧式气化器 -- process heat, not electric power per the SOP's thermal/electric distinction) with no mention of any on-site electricity-generating plant.
confirmed_how: Shandong Energy Regulatory Office (a National Energy Administration provincial office -- primary/regulatory source) states the 110kV transmission and dock works were both in the pre-construction preparation stage together, i.e. the terminal's electricity supply is via a purpose-built grid transmission line, not on-site generation. The terminal's own EIA approval document lists only submerged-combustion vaporizers (process heat via gas combustion, explicitly a thermal, not electric, use per SOP guidance) among its combustion sources, with no generator/turbine mentioned anywhere in the approval's exhaustive facilities list.
